more.summary: In 2016, a binary star system emitting unusually strong gamma rays was discovered in our galactic neighborhood. Now, astronomers have found the smoking gun, or rather, a smoking trail of cool molecular gas that suggests jets emanating from a microquasar—one of the few known outside the Milky Way—are responsible.

more.title: Different transcription systems shape chromatin behavior in distinct nuclear regions
more.summary: Inside the cell nucleus, DNA is wrapped around histone proteins to form nucleosomes, which are further organized into chromatin. Chromatin has traditionally been divided into transcriptionally active euchromatin and relatively inactive heterochromatin. However, chromatin is not a fixed structure.

more.title: Rare meteorite from Mars gives us a view into its ancient crust
more.author: Jacek Krywko
more.summary: A meteorite found in the Sahara is a rare piece of Mars' ancient crust.

more.title: Satlyt takes another step toward turning satellites into space data centers
more.author: Dominic-Madori Davis
more.summary: Satlyt ran a successful test this month bringing it closer to turning spacecraft, starting with satellites, into virtual data centers.

more.title: Scientists develop new system to boost prime editing in dicot plants
more.summary: A new gene-editing system could make it easier for researchers to introduce precise genetic changes into crops such as tomatoes, soybeans and rapeseed. Developed by researchers in China, SmartPE improves prime editing efficiency in several dicot plants, addressing a major limitation of the technique.

more.title: Scientists reveal a hidden snakebite crisis killing up to 513,000 people a year
more.summary: A startling new study suggests that venomous snakebites are killing far more people worldwide than official statistics indicate, with an estimated 274,000 to 513,000 deaths every year. Researchers found that as many as 7 million people could suffer snake envenoming annually, while more than 800,000 survivors are left with long-term disabilities.

more.title: Figuring out where cosmic neutrinos come from is tricky—radio telescopes could help find 'ghost particles' origin
more.summary: Neutrinos are funny little particles that weigh almost nothing, making them one of the universe's most elusive building blocks. They can come from objects as mundane as bananas and as exotic as supernovas—the exploding death throes of massive stars. Most neutrinos stream through space and pass through the Earth without interacting with anything.

more.title: Salesforce’s M&A spree continues with a reported $375M deal for defense tech startup Rune
more.author: Marina Temkin
more.summary: The AI logistics startup will bolster the CRM giant's Missionforce defense platform.

more.title: Ollie, a privacy-focused AI assistant, is shutting down
more.author: Lucas Ropek
more.summary: As an increasing number of AI assistants flood the market, the founder of Ollie, an assistant that respected its users' privacy, says it will be shutting down in a week.

more.title: Astronauts just gave the International Space Station a powerful upgrade
more.summary: Two astronauts completed a 7-hour, 11-minute spacewalk to install a new solar array on the International Space Station, bringing NASA one step closer to a major power upgrade. Once the final array is installed on November 5, the station will have up to 30% more available power, supporting critical operations and its eventual controlled deorbit.

more.title: Livestock guardian dogs enlisted in efforts to conserve Texas' smallest fox
more.summary: In the Texas Panhandle, two livestock guardian dogs patrol a herd of cattle grazing the Rita Blanca National Grasslands. Although their singular focus is protecting the herd from would-be predators, their presence may make them wildlife conservation allies.

more.title: New home for orangutans rescued from Indonesia's burning forests
more.summary: Deep in a forest in Indonesian Borneo, conservationists open a cage. A female orangutan and her baby waste little time, clambering up the towering trees and disappearing into the canopy, safe at last.

more.title: For many, striped bass fishing is a way of life. But the iconic species could face collapse
more.summary: Striped bass fishing has been Bill Jakob's passion for more than 60 years, and he remembers an era when he'd spend all night casting his line into the crashing waves off Montauk and get eight or nine fish ranging up to 40 pounds (18 kilograms), a big catch by anyone's standards.

more.title: Chemists create disappearing tattoos: Here's the science behind how they work
more.summary: How handy would it be if you could make your tattoos invisible for a job interview in the morning, and reveal them again for a party in the evening? This sounds like science fiction, but it may soon be reality.

more.title: Are narcissists multiplying or is the social media algorithm making them bolder? The answer in five stages
more.summary: Social media doesn't necessarily reflect who you are, but it may intensify particular personality traits and confirm or even persuade you that your worst behavior is justified.

more.title: Tiny photonic chip links telescopes together to view the universe in 'astonishing' detail
more.summary: A tiny glass chip developed by researchers at Heriot-Watt University has linked two telescopes together to enable them to act as a single powerful instrument, marking an important step toward a new generation of astronomical technology.

more.title: Meta strikes deal to help bring a low-carbon cement plant to Missouri
more.author: Maria Gallucci
more.summary: Tech companies say they're seeking low-carbon construction materials to limit the climate impact of their data centers.
